correctness.rationale: Closed Hamming balls of radius exactly 2 in {0,1}^d are the hypotheses (centers), and point queries are classified by distance≤2. For any hypothetical five-query VC-shattered set, translate an all-positive center to zero, forcing query supports of size≤2. Identifying coordinates by nonzero 5-bit incidence column yields exactly 7260 bounded-multiplicity normal forms, and any center making a positive response uses ≤4 coordinates and at most two outside the union; independently implemented C++ exhaustive enumeration found at most 26 of 31 nonzero response patterns. Hence VC≤4 in ALL dimensions, with explicit four-query witnesses. An all-dimensional online upper5 follows by restricting first positive branch to centers of weight≤2, then classifying exceptional one-/two-weight query branches via singleton and star subfamilies of Ldim≤2. The exact depth-five certificate has 31 internal queries and 32 distinct centers, independently checked against every leaf path, giving Ldim5 for d≥6. Small d follow from branch counting and witnesses. Finite checks do not replace the general structural online argument.
residual_risks: The all-dimensional online dimension bound uses a symbolic branch-family lemma; bounded tests cannot by themselves prove it.
Exact-distance-two shells are different from closed radius-two balls.

originality.rationale: Adler–Benediktsson–Macpherson treat ordinary Hamming graph adjacency (distance 1) and Johnson neighborhoods, not closed radius2 balls. Guingona et al. show VC=Ldim for specified families of linear zero sets, whose hypotheses differ. Ghazi et al. prove broad dimension closure estimates, not exact sharp values for this metric-ball class. Relevant Resultary Hamming ball results concern Fourier/Turán positivity and distance shells, not online shattering. The claimed full dimension sequence and first gap are not implied by these known statements.

value.rationale: Closed radius-two Hamming balls form a canonical Boolean metric range space. The exact all-d VC and Littlestone dimensions and their first separation at d6 yield an intrinsic threshold for offline vs online complexity, and the uniform stabilization is surprising given 2^d centers. Its complete certificates and symbolic upper bound make it a natural classification rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
residual_risks: No claims for other alphabet sizes, radii, or exact-distance spheres.

scientific_limitations: Binary Hamming cubes only; closed radius2 balls.
All dimensions d≥1, with all-dimensional structural bounds and finite d6 witness.
